subject: surgery
title: Advanced Trauma Life Support, primary survey, definitive airway, and lethal triad
refs: ATLS Advanced Trauma Life Support 10th ed

steps.tx: The Advanced Trauma Life Support primary survey organizes resuscitation into an orderly sequence designed to rapidly identify and treat immediately life-threatening **injuries**. The survey follows the ABCDE mnemonic: airway with cervical spine motion restriction, breathing and ventilation, circulation with hemorrhage control, disability and neurological status, and exposure with environmental hypothermia prevention. Resuscitative interventions occur concurrently with assessment, and deterioration at any stage mandates immediate reversion to airway re-evaluation.
steps.say: The ATLS primary survey follows the ABCDE sequence: airway with cervical protection, breathing, circulation with hemorrhage control, neurological disability, and environmental exposure. Deterioration mandates immediate return to airway re-evaluation.

rows: Chin lift, jaw thrust, endotracheal tube
Warm blankets, fluid warmers, room control

steps.tx: Establishing a definitive airway is indicated for apnea, severe neurological depression with Glasgow Coma Scale score of eight or **less**, impending airway compromise from inhalation burns, severe maxillofacial fractures, or inability to maintain oxygenation. Endotracheal intubation with rapid sequence induction and in-line manual cervical stabilization represents the primary approach. When endotracheal intubation fails or is anatomically impossible, surgical cricothyroidotomy through the cricothyroid membrane provides emergency surgical access in adults, whereas needle cricothyroidotomy is preferred in children under twelve.
steps.say: Definitive airway placement is indicated for coma with GCS eight or less, apnea, or severe facial trauma. Endotracheal intubation with manual in-line cervical stabilization is first-line, followed by surgical cricothyroidotomy if intubation fails.

nodes.label: Rapid sequence intubation with C-spine control

steps.tx: Hemorrhagic shock is the leading preventable cause of early post-injury death. The five anatomical compartments capable of hiding major internal **bleeding** are the chest, abdomen, pelvis, retroperitoneum with long-bone fractures, and the external scene floor. Hemostatic resuscitation avoids excessive crystalloid infusion, employing early balanced blood component therapy utilizing packed red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, and platelets in an equal one-to-one-to-one ratio alongside intravenous tranexamic acid administered within three hours of injury.
steps.say: Hemorrhagic shock is assessed across five major compartments: chest, abdomen, pelvis, retroperitoneum, and floor. Resuscitation avoids crystalloids, prioritizing balanced one-to-one-to-one blood components and tranexamic acid within three hours.

rows: Dullness to percussion / hemothorax on X-ray
Abdominal distension / fluid on FAST scan

steps.tx: The lethal triad of trauma comprises hypothermia, metabolic acidosis, and coagulopathy, creating a self-reinforcing vicious physiological **cycle** that drives cellular shock and microvascular failure. Resuscitation room hypothermia impairs platelet aggregation and enzymatic clotting cascades, worsening hemorrhage and hypoperfusion. Damage control surgery interrupts this lethal spiral by prioritizing rapid operative control of active exsanguination and enteric contamination, temporary abdominal wall closure, and transfer to the intensive care unit for physiological correction.
steps.say: The lethal triad of hypothermia, acidosis, and coagulopathy drives mortality in severe trauma. Damage control surgery interrupts this cycle by rapidly controlling bleeding and contamination, delaying definitive reconstruction until physiological stabilization.

right.title: Damage Control Surgery
points: Pack bleeding liver & staple hollow viscera
Temporary abdominal closure with negative pressure
ICU resuscitation of warmth & pH prior to re-exploration
